origin.usage: na.locf0(object, fromLast = FALSE, maxgap = Inf, coredata = NULL)

arguments.name: fromLast
arguments.text: Carry the next observation backward when TRUE.

arguments.name: maxgap
arguments.text: Runs longer than maxgap stay missing.

arguments.name: coredata
arguments.text: When TRUE, fill the values and keep the original index. Zoo objects do this by default.

origin.details: The workhorse behind na.locf. It does not trim leading NAs, which is the same as na.rm FALSE. A leading gap stays missing and is repeated until the first observation.
origin.value: c(1, NA, 3, NA, NA) returns 1, 1, 3, 3, 3. There is no leading gap to keep.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(zoo))
stopifnot(packageVersion("zoo") == "1.9-1")
x <- na.locf0(c(1, NA, 3, NA, NA))
cat(paste(vapply(as.numeric(x), function(v) if (is.nan(v)) "NaN" else if (is.na(v)) "NA" else sprintf("%.12g", v), ""), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
